theme.title: Full-Court Mix
theme.subtitle: Teams, stars and stories from across basketball
theme.recap: The best numbers come from all over basketball history. Which answer surprised you most?

questions.prompt: In only their third season, how many games did the 1970–71 Bucks win?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Milwaukee posted a 66–16 record in only its third year of existence

funFacts.text: The arrival of Oscar Robertson gave young star Lew Alcindor a legendary partner.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: A key part of this championship season was the acquisition of Oscar Robertson

funFacts.text: Milwaukee beat the Baltimore Bullets in a four-game Finals sweep to win its first title.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: They faced off against the Baltimore Bullets and swept them in four games

funFacts.text: Role players included Lucius Allen, Bob Boozer and Dick Cunningham behind the star pairing.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: key reserves such as Lucius Allen, Bob Boozer and Dick Cunningham

questions.prompt: Michael Jordan set a playoff scoring record against the 1986 Celtics in a loss. How many points did he score?
questions.note: 63 points, a playoff record, in a Bulls loss.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Michael Jordan (63)

funFacts.text: Chicago needed two overtimes to settle the record-setting game in Boston, but the Celtics held on.
Charles Oakley led the Bulls on the glass that night, pulling down fourteen rebounds.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Charles Oakley (14)

funFacts.text: Boston Garden drew a crowd of 14,890 for that historic first-round playoff game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Boston Garden 14,890

questions.prompt: Reggie Miller retired in 2005 as the career leader in threes. How many had he made?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: eventually retiring with a record 2,560 three-pointers made.

funFacts.text: Miller overtook Dale Ellis for the career lead in 1997, well before the modern three-point explosion.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: In 1997, Miller surpassed Ellis as the NBA's all-time leader in three-pointers

funFacts.text: During Miller's career, the NBA briefly shortened the three-point line for three seasons before restoring it.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: For three seasons beginning in 1994–95, the NBA attempted to address decreased scoring by shortening the distance

funFacts.text: The NBA's later three-point revolution is often credited to Stephen Curry and his unusually deep attempts.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Stephen Curry, who is credited with revolutionizing the game by inspiring teams to more heavily employ the three-point shot

questions.prompt: In the game that clinched the 1972 title, Wilt Chamberlain had 24 points and how many rebounds?
questions.context: 1972 NBA Finals · Game 5 · vs New York
questions.note: 29 rebounds, and the Finals MVP award.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Wilt Chamberlain scored 24 points and 29 rebounds and earned the NBA Finals MVP Award

funFacts.text: Chamberlain was listed as doubtful for the clincher with a sprained right wrist, yet played anyway.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Chamberlain was listed as doubtful for Game Five with a sprained right wrist

funFacts.text: ABC announcer Keith Jackson informally tallied Wilt's blocks before the NBA officially tracked them.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: ABC announcer Keith Jackson counted them up during the broadcast

funFacts.text: The victory delivered the Lakers' first championship since the franchise relocated from Minneapolis.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: win their sixth NBA title and their first since 1954, when the team was still based in Minneapolis

questions.prompt: In Victor Wembanyama's rookie year, San Antonio lost how many games in a row?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: lost 18 consecutive games between November 5 and December 15, the longest losing streak in franchise history.

funFacts.text: The Spurs won the draft lottery and made Victor Wembanyama their first overall selection.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: selecting French center Victor Wembanyama as their third #1 pick in franchise history

funFacts.text: San Antonio had previously used first overall picks on two future legends, David Robinson and Tim Duncan.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: after previously selecting Tim Duncan in 1997 and David Robinson in 1987

funFacts.text: Even with the much-hyped rookie, the Spurs missed the postseason for another year.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: were eliminated from playoff contention for the fifth consecutive season
